headline: Smith-Waterman catches prompt injections bioinformatics technique improves AI security
summary: New method detects AI prompt injections that regex misses, boosting security
details: The Smith-Waterman algorithm, originally from bioinformatics, has been adapted to detect AI prompt injections that evade traditional regex-based defenses. This technique uses a semantic substitution matrix to identify paraphrased attacks.

The method tokenizes incoming prompts and runs the Smith-Waterman algorithm to compare them against known attack templates, allowing for gaps and mismatches. This approach achieved a +34.5 F1 percentage points improvement over ML classifiers.
The implementation, called prompt-shield, is open-source and available on GitHub and PyPI under Apache 2.0. It includes 33 detectors, 9 output scanners, and 1040 tests.

headline_marked: [[MIRA: Multiplayer Interactive World Models]] Trained on Rocket League
headline: MIRA: Multiplayer Interactive World Models Trained on Rocket League
summary: MIRA is a new multiplayer interactive world model, specifically trained using the complex physics of Rocket League. This development aims to advance AI's ability to predict and interact in dynamic, multi-agent environments.
details: MIRA is a new project focused on creating Multiplayer Interactive World Models. It has been specifically trained using data from the popular video game Rocket League.

The concept of a multiplayer world model has been described as a 'dream' for games like Rocket League, which feature complex physics and dynamic multi-agent interactions. MIRA aims to tackle this challenge.

This research explores how AI can better understand and predict outcomes in highly interactive and unpredictable virtual environments. Such models are crucial for advancing AI's ability to operate in complex, real-world scenarios.
